subject.title: Feature request: opt-in per-domain credential pass-through for web_fetch/image tools

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared core exact-host credential policy for web_fetch and image URLs, or keep generic tools anonymous and require an explicit plugin-owned authenticated media tool?
rationale: Source inspection proves the capability is missing but cannot decide whether generic agent URL tools should receive credentials; that choice defines a new secret-routing, SSRF, configuration, and plugin-ownership contract.

options.title: Shared guarded core policy
options.body: Add one opt-in SecretRef-backed exact-HTTPS-host policy reused by web_fetch and image loading, with cross-origin stripping and security tests.

options.title: Explicit plugin tool
options.body: Keep built-in tools anonymous and let a plugin expose a clearly named authenticated fetch or media tool with its own host policy.

options.title: No new credential path
options.body: Retain authenticated shell or service-specific workflows and avoid expanding credential access from generic agent tools.

recommendation.title: Shared guarded core policy
recommendation.body: Add one opt-in SecretRef-backed exact-HTTPS-host policy reused by web_fetch and image loading, with cross-origin stripping and security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current web-fetch, image, guarded-network, and provider surfaces that this decision would change.
